newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures settled weaker on Thursday, driven deeper by stronger-than-expected German M3 money supply data, while renewed domestic investor interest gave a lift to longer-dated bonds in the cash market.
Marked curve flattening seen on Wednesday continued through Thursday, with traders saying long-dated bonds with the coupons stripped off were still in demand.
The spread between 10- and 30-year bonds narrowed two basis points while the five- to 10-year spread flattened five basis points, after a move of similar magnitude yesterday.

"There's definitely the sensation people are going longer along the curve," said a trader at a French bank. "Dollar strength is still the order of the day. The last 24 hours has seen an important move in the market."

Domestic buyers followed foreign buyers into the long end of in search of higher returns, with buying strong from the 2007 OAT onwards due to lack of paper of this maturity, and also in 2019, 2023 and 2025 paper.
"When you compare with the German curve, there's still room for flattening in France," said another trader.
The bond future closed two basis points lower and the March PIBOR contract too suffered for a second day as dollar strength helped take the edge off hopes of speedy rate cuts in France.

German December M3 money supply came in slightly higher than expected, with the Bundesbank announcing an annualised growth rate of 7.9 percent compared with its average level in the final quarter of 1995. It grew 8.1 percent in the last quarter of 1996 versus the fourth quarter the year before.
